answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because zephyr only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, fable is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
